title: The same approval publication change lets verified legacy SHA-named reports record approval and merge

consumerGuidance.architecture: MARC's trusted controller is Node.js CommonJS with no runtime dependencies. Legacy SHA-named report evidence without reportCreatedAt remains unchanged and verifiable; never rename history. Operator approval may be supplied to merge after the report pair is published.
consumerGuidance.notes: Reduced from PR16 to the two controller files that own approval publication; the other PR16 files do not affect this behavior.

forbiddenFindings.example: Claiming legacy SHA-named reports can no longer record approval or merge, although the guard is gone and verifyReportCommit reproduces and verifies their bytes.
Reporting the documented non-atomic GitHub description update in record-approval as a defect, or asking for a different receipt hash algorithm.

notes: Counterpart to legacy-report-approval-merge: identical except that the reportCreatedAt guard is removed, so verifyReportCommit decides for legacy evidence and fails closed on any other head movement. Version 2 replaces a merge-only exemption, which still stranded legacy PRs at record-approval.
